To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

LAMP-1 is an integral membrane glycoprotein of lysosomes that translocates to the surface membrane of activated platelets, and that LAMP- 2 is also expressed on the surface of thrombin-activated platelets.
we identified a new platelet surface glyco protein that translocates from a membrane compartment of the platelet to the surface membrane upon activation.
the lysosome-associated membrane proteins LAMP-1 (CD-107) and LAMP-2 translocate from the lysosome to the platelet surface membrane in response to platelets activation by a variety of agonists.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the platelet surface glycopeptide(s) responsible for the binding of the monoclonal antibody, PAC-1.
the identification of platelet surface glycoconjugates that are expressed on activated platelets and are involved in the adhesive and prothrombotics phenotype of these cells.
the identification of novel platelet surface proteins that may play a role as adhesion molecules or as receptors in the process of platelet aggregation and thrombosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LAMP-1 is a marker for activated platelets and LAMP-2 is a marker for thrombin-activated platelets.
LAMP-1 (CD107a) and LAMP-2 (CD107b) are expressed on the surface membrane of activated platelets.
lysosome-associated membrane proteins 1 and 2 are translocated from the lysosomal compartment to the surface of activated, but not resting, platelets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified and cloned a cDNA for a lysosome-associated membrane glycoprotein that is translocated to the cell surface when platelets are stimulated by a strong thrombin agonist.
the LAMP proteins are lysosomal membrane proteins that are expressed on the surface of stimulated platelets and are involved in the adhesive and prothrombotie phenotype of these cells
we have identified two lysosomal proteins that translocate from the lysosomal compartment to the surface when the platelets are activated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LAMP-1 is a platelet-specific marker of platelet activation.
LAMP-1 is a platelet activation marker that is expressed on the platelet surface membrane in response to strong agonists.
the lysosome-associated membrane proteins, LAMP-1 (CD107a), LAMP-2 (CD107b), LAMP-3 (CD63) and LAMP-4 (CD68), are expressed in a regulated fashion in the platelet plasma membrane.
